newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares moving downwards before Fed.
newsitem.headline: German shares moving downwards before Fed.

text.p: German shares opened lower on Monday and were seen stuck in very narrow trading ranges on uncertainty ahead of Tuesday's meeting of U.S. Federal Reserve officials to consider U.S. interest rates.
The DAX index of Germany's leading 30 shares stood 15.46 points lower at 2,630.64 in early trade amid volumes described by dealers as very thin.
"People are holding off ahead of the Fed and are generally unwilling to buy at these levels," said one trader, referring to the record highs reached by German shares in recent days.
The continued strength of the dollar, trading at around 1.5165 to the mark, was however seen as limiting any downward moves of the DAX to 2,620 at the lowest.
Some traders said the market had already factored in a small increase in U.S. rates.
"People are expecting a rise of perhaps 25 basis points. That wouldn't be a problem for the market," one said.
But even dollar-sensitive chemical shares were unable to buck the downwards trend, with only Hoechst holding ground at 55.27 marks, a bare two pfennigs higher.
Insurance group Munich Re held up fairly well on its DAX 30 debut given the market conditions, falling just three marks to 3,447.00 marks.
